title: Unary doubled prefix characterization
statement: For every binary word $x$ and $n\in\mathbb N$, the following are equivalent: at each pair of positions $2i,2i+1$ for $0\le i<n$, both bits of $x$ are $1$, and the next pair is $01$; or the first $n$ bits of the word encoded by those doubled positions are all $1$, with the separator $01$ immediately afterward. In all indexed-bit statements, a position beyond the end of $x$ is read as $0$.
caveat: The equivalence is between two definitions of the same indexed-bit conditions; the second clause is best read as the doubled-prefix predicate applied to the word $1^n$.
